title.narrative: A fair price for smallholder farmers to reduce the living income gap in Indonesia

description.narrative: The project ‘A fair price for smallholder farmers to reduce the living income gap in Indonesia’ aims at supporting fair pricing of RSPO certified palm oil fresh fruit bunches (FFBs) for smallholder farmers in north Sumatra and SE Sulawesi, Indonesia. Fair pricing is one of many drivers to support reducing the living income gap. The project pays special attention to women and youth to respond to inequalities faced due to age and/or gender. The project will work along the palm oil value chain: with farmer cooperatives, middlemen, and mills in Indonesia, with international retailer in the Netherlands, AS Watson Benelux, and towards lobbying the Roundtable for Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO). Together the consortium will learn where the problems exist and how everyone can be part of the solution to shift value and power closer to smallholder farmers and their communities. As this project is also designed to be a systems change project, there are different levels of impact envisioned. At the grassroots level, we aim for women, men, and youth and smallholder farmers to be empowered with data and knowledge about their economic rights and ways to close the living income gap. At the regency or provincial level, the ambition is for local authorities to institute a higher farmgate price for FFBs so that it becomes institutionalized. At the same time, the ambition at the Dutch level is for AS Watson Benelux to learn where unfair pricing exists in their palm oil chain and how to use their leverage to influence other palm oil retailers to lift up the sector. At the global level, the goal is to lobby the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil to include requirements on living income in their certification standards, also known as their Principles & Criteria. Currently there are no requirements to pay a living income to farmers in the RSPO standards.
